prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Kansas City Missouri for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist — the right provider depends on your specific needs (single tooth vs. full-arch, bone loss, medical history), your location in the Kansas City area, and what matters most to you (experience, price, comfort, speed). Instead of naming one person, here’s a practical way to find the best implant provider for you and what to look for in Kansas City, MO.

Who to consider
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons or periodontists: they place the implants most often and handle difficult cases (bone grafting, extractions, sedation). Prosthodontists specialize in the restorations and are a good choice if you need complex prosthetic work.
- Experienced general dentists with advanced implant training can be excellent for straightforward cases.

How to find candidates
- Use directories: American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID), American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS), American Academy of Periodontology (AAP), and ADA “Find a dentist.”
- Check local reviews (Google, Yelp) and look for before/after photos rather than relying only on star ratings.
- Ask your general dentist for referrals — they often know the best local specialists and which ones collaborate well on prosthetic work.

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants do you place per year? How many like my case?
- What is your formal implant training and certifications?
- Do you use CBCT (3D imaging) and guided implant planning?
- Who will do the final crown/bridge — you or a prosthodontist — and who coordinates the treatment?
- What implant system do you use and why? Do you offer warranties or maintenance programs?
- What are the risks, alternatives, estimated timeline, and total cost (including grafts, temporary restorations, and prosthesis)?
- Do you offer sedation or anesthesia if needed?
- Can you show before/after cases and provide patient references?

Red flags
- No formal training or few implant cases.
- No 3D imaging for complex planning.
- Refusal to provide a clear written treatment plan or total cost.
- Poor communication or no follow-up care plan.
